cycle.note: 80 hours in the two-year period immediately preceding license expiration; each year of the period measured back from the expiration date.

requirements.label: Non-technical
requirements.note: Maximum, not a target. Because 40 of the 80 hours must be technical, at most 40 non-technical hours can count toward the 80.

requirements.label: Ethics
requirements.note: 4 hours of technical ethics (codes of conduct, ethical dilemmas, case studies). We count Regulatory Ethics courses; Behavioral Ethics is non-technical in California and doesn't count toward these 4.

requirements.label: Board-approved Regulatory Review course
requirements.note: Required if more than six years have lapsed since the last one. Not interchangeable with ethics. Must carry a CBA approval number (RRL-/RRS-).

requirements.label: Accounting & auditing
requirements.note: Financial statement preparation, auditing, reviews, compilations, attestation and assurance; governmental accounting and auditing courses count too. Fraud courses don't count toward these hours. Not needed if you also do government audits — the government hours cover A&A.

coveredNotes.government_audit: CBA: "If you fulfill the governmental auditing CE requirement, you are deemed to have met the A&A CE requirement."

requirements.label: Governmental accounting & auditing
requirements.note: Fraud courses don't count toward these hours. Meeting this and the fraud requirement also covers the A&A requirement.

requirements.label: Preparation engagement subject matter
requirements.note: 8 hours in preparation engagement subject matter. Covered by the A&A or government hours if you also do that work.

coveredNotes.attest: CBA: "If you fulfill the A&A CE requirement, you are deemed to have met the preparation engagement CE requirement."
coveredNotes.government_audit: CBA: "If you fulfill the governmental auditing CE requirement, you are deemed to have met the A&A CE requirement" — and A&A covers preparation engagements.

requirements.label: Fraud
requirements.note: 4 hours of fraud CE on top of the A&A, government or preparation-engagement hours (16 CCR 87(f)): the first 4 fraud hours count only here. Fraud hours beyond 4 can also count toward A&A or government when the course's field fits. One requirement, not one per activity.

newLicensee.note: First renewal only: 20 hours for each full six months from license issue to first expiration (none if under six full months). Half technical, including the 2-hour Regulatory Review. No yearly minimums. Ethics and fraud apply only once the full 80 hours is required.

requirements.label: Technical subject matter
requirements.note: Half of your hours must be technical. The Regulatory Review course counts toward this.

requirements.label: Non-technical
requirements.note: Maximum, not a target. Because half your hours must be technical, only this many non-technical hours can count.

requirements.label: Board-approved Regulatory Review course
requirements.note: Required for every new licensee's first renewal. Must carry a CBA approval number (RRL-/RRS-).

requirements.label: Accounting & auditing
requirements.note: 6 hours for every 20 hours required. Fraud courses don't count toward these hours. Not needed if you also do government audits — the government hours cover A&A.

coveredNotes.government_audit: CBA: "If you fulfill the governmental auditing CE requirement, you are deemed to have met the A&A CE requirement."

requirements.label: Preparation engagement subject matter
requirements.note: 2 hours for every 20 hours required. Covered by the A&A or government hours if you also do that work.

coveredNotes.attest: CBA: "If you fulfill the A&A CE requirement, you are deemed to have met the preparation engagement CE requirement."
coveredNotes.government_audit: CBA: "If you fulfill the governmental auditing CE requirement, you are deemed to have met the A&A CE requirement" — and A&A covers preparation engagements.

requirements.label: Fraud
requirements.note: 4 hours of fraud CE on top of the A&A, government or preparation-engagement hours (16 CCR 87(f)): the first 4 fraud hours count only here. Fraud hours beyond 4 can also count toward A&A or government when the course's field fits. One requirement, not one per activity.

toVerify: Exact CA mapping of NASBA fields of study to technical vs non-technical (esp. Business Management and Organization, Computer Software and Applications).
How CA treats fractional NASBA credits (e.g. 1.8) given the CBA template's half-hour increment rule.

Behavioral Ethics: CBA lists it as non-technical and requires 'technical ethics', so we don't count it toward the 4 ethics hours. A Behavioral Ethics course whose content is a code of conduct review might still qualify.

Fraud hours beyond the required 4 counting toward A&A/government: 87(f) excludes the required fraud CE from (c)-(e); we read that as letting extra fraud hours count (Nazim's call, 2026-09-30). Earliest fraud courses fill the 4 first.
